title: The working harbour inside today's visitor landscape
dek: A source-linked sequence for interpreting how quays, infrastructure and city streets met before the contemporary Vieux-Port took shape.

chapters.title: Read the working harbour
chapters.intro: The 1925 and 1962 views place the quays inside a larger city and river system. They can orient a visitor without flattening the site into nostalgia.

chapters.title: Quays, movement and connection
chapters.intro: The 1963 and 1965 report sequences bring the Clock Tower area, warehouses, quay structures and connecting infrastructure into a traceable research frame.

chapters.title: Where port met city
chapters.intro: Rue de la Commune and Bonsecours make the threshold tangible at street level. Place d'Armes connects that edge to the civic district beyond.

chapters.title: Before the visitor district
chapters.intro: The 1980 hangar report names a transition that can be investigated, sourced and interpreted in the places where that change is now experienced.

activations.title: Quay evidence route
activations.audience: Visitors moving between the Clock Tower area and rue de la Commune
activations.use: A short physical and mobile sequence linking quay infrastructure to the street that served it.
activations.dependency: Exact viewpoint verification, site operations review and rights clearance.

activations.title: Port layers at a visitor threshold
activations.audience: Visitors arriving at an orientation point or seasonal installation
activations.use: A controlled comparison of 1925, 1962 and 1980, with source and uncertainty visible beside each image.
activations.dependency: Production files, bilingual copy and installation approval.

activations.title: Project memory packet
activations.use: A compact evidence packet that can travel with future signage, exhibition or programming briefs.
activations.dependency: A named internal owner and an approved evidence-review workflow.

nextStep: Review one quay-to-street route with the interpretation and public-realm teams, then identify the four records worth taking to production resolution.
